newsitem.title: SURINAM: Suriname sees 4 pct growth, 6 pct inflation in '97.
newsitem.headline: Suriname sees 4 pct growth, 6 pct inflation in '97.

text.p: Suriname's economy is expected to grow by four percent in 1997, with inflation rising to six percent for the year, Central Bank President Henk Goedschalk said on Tuesday.
"This year we will see inflation of around six percent....The economy will grow. The forecast is around four percent," he said in an interview with Reuters.
A stable currency and balanced budget helped slow inflation to less than one percent in 1996 from 36 percent the previous year.

Accumulated inflation for the first quarter of 1997 stood at 2.2 percent, said Goedschalk, who took over as head of the Central Bank soon after the election of President Jules Wijdenbosch in September.
Suriname's economy grew by three percent in 1996 and the four percent target for 1997 was exactly in line with a recent International Monetary Fund (IMF) forecast.

Still, the IMF forecast that inflation would rise to 20 percent in 1997 because of the planned introduction of a 15 percent value-added tax on July 1, the elimination of electricity and water service tariffs and substantial public-sector pay rises.

Despite the 50 percent pay award to civil servants made earlier this year, Goedschalk said the government's 1997 budget was broadly balanced. The fiscal deficit would be no larger than one percent of gross domestic product, he said.
Suriname's National Assembly is due to start debating the budget Wednesday.

A structural adjustment program based on fiscal discipline saw the former Dutch colony's economy begin to stabilize in 1995 after several years of economic contraction and inflation of up to 600 percent.
